hunks.baseline: Jinho delivered the verdict with the solemnity of a judge. He was the manager of the goshiwon[^1] where I lived, a thirty-year-old exam candidate.
hunks.sol: Jinho hyung delivered the verdict with the solemnity of a judge. He was the manager of the goshiwon[^1] where I lived, a thirty-year-old exam candidate.

hunks.baseline: We were fairly close, only three years apart, and I remembered how he was always going on about how much he knew about IT. That was why I showed him the capsule I’d picked up, but…
hunks.sol: We were fairly close, being only three years apart, and he was always bragging about how much he knew about IT. That was why I’d shown him the capsule I’d picked up, but…

hunks.baseline: Just as I’d said, he hadn’t even looked inside. He’d merely given it a quick once-over, top to bottom, before declaring it garbage. Since I’d been thinking about how much I could get for it secondhand, the blow hit me hard.
hunks.sol: Just as I’d said, he hadn’t even looked inside. He’d merely given it a quick once-over, top to bottom, before declaring it garbage. Since I’d been wondering how much I could get for it secondhand, the blow hit me hard.

hunks.baseline: “Jinho…”
hunks.sol: “Hyung…”

hunks.baseline: I wanted to kill him. My fist trembled with the urge, and Jinho flinched. Unlike him, who had spent his entire life hunched over a desk, I had a fairly intimidating build.
hunks.sol: I wanted to kill him. My fist trembled with the urge, and Jinho hyung flinched. Unlike him, who had spent his entire life hunched over a desk, I had a fairly intimidating build.

hunks.baseline: “Taekyung. Let’s recall Article 1, Clause 12 of the Awakened Persons Special Act. What you’re about to do falls under assault of a civilian by an Awakened…”
hunks.sol: “Taekyung. Let’s recall Article 1, Clause 12 of the Awakened Persons Special Act. What you’re about to do constitutes assault of a civilian by an Awakened…”

hunks.baseline: F-rank. The lowest possible grade, with no particular talent to speak of, but I prided myself on having worked hard. With what I earned, I paid for my mother’s medical treatment and supported my only younger sibling.
hunks.sol: F-rank. The lowest possible rank, with no particular talent to speak of, but I prided myself on having worked hard. With what I earned, I paid for my mother’s medical treatment and supported my only younger sibling.

hunks.baseline: I gave a short laugh at Jinho’s flustered expression.
hunks.sol: I gave a short laugh at Jinho hyung’s flustered expression.

hunks.baseline: “Then buy me a drink. This is when you’re supposed to act like my big brother.”
hunks.sol: “Then buy me a drink. This is when you’re supposed to act like my hyung.”

hunks.baseline: “Listen to the disrespect on you. Try treating me like your big brother before you say something like that.”
hunks.sol: “Listen to the disrespect on you. Try treating me like your hyung before you say something like that.”

hunks.baseline: He said that, but still jerked his chin for me to follow. From his expression, we were going to drink until one of us fell over tonight.
hunks.sol: He said that, but still jerked his chin for me to follow. Judging by his expression, we were getting plastered tonight.

hunks.baseline: A Gate marks the boundary of the world. Outside it—in other words, in the modern world—is the civilized society we know. Go inside, though, and it’s crawling with monsters no one has ever seen or heard of.
hunks.sol: A Gate marks the boundary between worlds. Outside it—in other words, in the modern world—is the civilized society we know. Go inside, though, and it’s crawling with monsters no one has ever seen or heard of.

hunks.baseline: The weakest and most common of them were goblins—even an F-rank Hunter like me could handle one.
hunks.sol: The weakest and most common of them are goblins—even an F-rank Hunter like me can handle one.

hunks.baseline: Was that thing human or a monster? Leaning against a utility pole and vomiting, Jinho looked just like a goblin that had taken a hard blow to the solar plexus.
hunks.sol: Was that thing human or a monster? Leaning against a utility pole and vomiting, Jinho hyung looked just like a goblin that had taken a hard blow to the solar plexus.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, Jinho. Mr. Seong Jinho. Try to come to your senses.”
hunks.sol: “Hey, Jinho hyung. Mr. Seong Jinho. Try to come to your senses.”

hunks.baseline: He had been pounding drinks like a lunatic from the very first round, and this was how he’d ended up. Never mind that I’d had to pay the bill—I was soaked through after carrying the dead-drunk man all the way back to the goshiwon.
hunks.sol: He’d been pounding drinks like a lunatic since the first round, and this was how he’d ended up. Never mind that I’d had to pay the bill—I was soaked through after carrying the dead-drunk man all the way back to the goshiwon.

hunks.baseline: Sweat was a given. Vomit was extra. It was obvious whose it was.
hunks.sol: Sweat came standard. Vomit was an optional extra. There was no question whose mouth it had come from.

hunks.baseline: While he retched intermittently in the background, I watched the sun sink toward the horizon.
hunks.sol: With his intermittent retching as background music, I watched the sun sink toward the horizon.

hunks.baseline: *What a day this is turning out to be.*
hunks.sol: *What a spectacular day.*

hunks.baseline: You were the highlight of it all.
hunks.sol: And you were the highlight of it all.

hunks.baseline: “Home? My home’s in Gangwon Province. Oh, Mom. Mom! I want some of my mom’s doenjang stew[^2].”
hunks.sol: “Home? My home’s in Gangwon Province. Oh, Mom. Mom! I want some of my mom’s doenjang stew.[^2]”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, for crying out loud. It’s the goshiwon, Jinho.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, for crying out loud. It’s the goshiwon, hyung.”

hunks.baseline: “I feel gross.”
hunks.sol: “I still feel filthy.”

hunks.baseline: I went straight to the shower room in the goshiwon and showered for thirty minutes, but I still felt as if the smell of vomit were clinging to the tip of my nose.
hunks.sol: I went straight to the goshiwon’s shower room and washed for thirty minutes, but I could still smell vomit clinging to the tip of my nose.

hunks.baseline: When I returned, sniffing all the way, two nuisances were waiting in my room.
hunks.sol: When I returned to my room, sniffing all the way, two nuisances were waiting for me.

hunks.baseline: One was Jinho, dead drunk, and the other was…
hunks.sol: One was Jinho hyung, dead drunk, and the other was…

hunks.baseline: The capsule. I’d left the refrigerator-sized thing in my room, barely ten square meters, and it felt as if it had filled the entire space. I retreated onto the bed and began wondering what to do with it.
hunks.sol: The capsule. I’d left the refrigerator-sized thing in my room, barely ten square meters, and it felt as though it took up the entire space. I retreated onto the bed and began wondering what to do with it.

hunks.baseline: *Should I take it back where I found it?*
hunks.sol: *Should I take it back and throw it away?*

hunks.baseline: *I thought it was a fairly useful piece of equipment.*
hunks.sol: *I thought it might actually be useful.*

hunks.baseline: Shit, huh? Was it really that much of a piece of junk?
hunks.sol: Garbage, huh? Was it really that much of a wreck?

hunks.baseline: Come to think of it, I hadn’t even looked inside. Curiosity got the better of me, and I examined the capsule.
hunks.sol: Come to think of it, I hadn’t even looked inside. Curiosity got the better of me, and I began examining the capsule.

hunks.baseline: The capsule’s surface was yellowed with nicotine or something, and rust seemed to have formed in places. Once I let go of my attachment and took a proper look, I understood what Jinho had meant.
hunks.sol: The capsule’s surface was stained yellow with nicotine or something, and rust seemed to have formed in places. Once I set aside my attachment and took a proper look, I understood what Jinho hyung had meant.

hunks.baseline: I pressed the lone button sticking out, and the lid opened to reveal the interior. I had expected something impressive, but there was nothing much to see after all.
hunks.sol: I pressed the lone protruding button, and the lid opened to reveal the interior. I’d expected something impressive, but there was nothing much to see after all.

hunks.baseline: Did people really leave instruction manuals inside things they were throwing away? Especially in a piece of junk like this?
hunks.sol: Did people really leave instruction manuals inside things they were throwing away? Especially junk like this?

hunks.baseline: I skimmed the print without much thought until the manufacturing date stopped me.
hunks.sol: I skimmed the print without much thought until my eyes stopped on the manufacturing date.

hunks.baseline: *What kind of lunatic would have made a game machine on that day—no, during that period?*
hunks.sol: *What kind of lunatic would have been making a game machine on that day—no, during that period?*

hunks.baseline: *So that’s impossible.*
hunks.sol: *So there’s no way this can be right.*

hunks.baseline: Rather than read an instruction manual written by a lunatic, I might as well sleep. I pushed Jinho into a corner and closed my eyes.
hunks.sol: I’d be better off sleeping than reading some deranged instruction manual. I pushed Jinho hyung into a corner and closed my eyes.

hunks.baseline: The chair was hard. It had been made in 2020, so it was the same age as me. A twenty-seven-year-old chair. Its cushion had gone flat long ago.
hunks.sol: The chair was hard. It had been made in 2020, so it was the same age as me. The chair was a youthful twenty-seven. Its cushion had gone flat long ago.

hunks.baseline: That minor complaint vanished the moment I put on the helmet. A world of complete silence. A stillness without so much as a whisper of noise.
hunks.sol: That minor complaint vanished the moment I put on the helmet. A world of complete silence. Not so much as a whisper of noise.

hunks.baseline: But instead of sleep, my thoughts began to stir.
hunks.sol: But what followed wasn’t sleep. It was thought.

hunks.baseline: Hunters were certainly a highly paid profession, but that depended on your rank.
hunks.sol: Hunters were certainly well paid, but that depended on their rank.

hunks.baseline: F-rank Hunters like me were a dime a dozen, and unless you belonged to a Guild, you had to show up at a day-labor agency before dawn.
hunks.sol: F-rank Hunters like me were a dime a dozen, and unless you belonged to a Guild, you had to report to a day-labor agency before dawn.

hunks.baseline: Being unaffiliated was miserable. Government policy was never kind to unaffiliated Hunters, and the punishing tax rates imposed on Hunters were enough to take your breath away just hearing about them.
hunks.sol: Being unaffiliated was miserable. Government policy was never kind to unaffiliated Hunters, and the punishing tax rates imposed on Hunters were enough to leave you breathless just hearing about them.

hunks.baseline: Unlike me, my mother and younger sister lived in an apartment in a Safety Sector. It was an extravagant expense for an F-rank Hunter, but nothing mattered more to me than my family’s safety.
hunks.sol: Unlike me, my mother and younger sister lived in an apartment in a Safety Sector. It was an extravagant expense on an F-rank Hunter’s income, but nothing mattered more to me than my family’s safety.

hunks.baseline: Until now, I had barely managed to come up with enough money to renew their jeonse lease each year.[^3] But from now on… who knew?
hunks.sol: Until now, I had barely managed to scrape together enough money for each annual renewal of their jeonse lease.[^3] But from now on… who knew?

hunks.baseline: He had devoted himself to his family and was respected by society, but he died when I was seven.
hunks.sol: He had devoted himself to his family and was respected by everyone around him, but he died when I was seven.

hunks.baseline: Maybe it was the alcohol finally catching up with me. Maybe it was thinking about the past. Without realizing it, I went slack and my eyes began to close.
hunks.sol: Maybe the alcohol was finally catching up with me, or maybe it was because I was thinking about the past. Without realizing it, my body went slack and my eyes began to close.

hunks.baseline: As I surrendered to the wave of sleep pouring over me, I thought:
hunks.sol: As I surrendered to the wave of drowsiness washing over me, I thought:

hunks.baseline: Someone’s voice pierced my ears, but I didn’t care anymore. I slipped gently into sleep.
hunks.sol: Someone’s voice reached my ears, but I no longer cared. I drifted off to sleep.
